title: Equivariant Cohen coefficient extension and lift of a section
statement: Let $W$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with uniformizer $\pi$ and perfect residue field $k_0=W/\pi W$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $(C,\mathfrak n)$ be a complete Noetherian local $W$-algebra with local structure map and residue field $k'=C/\mathfrak n$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let a finite group $H$, of order invertible in $W$, act by local ring automorphisms on $W$ and $C$, compatibly with the structure map, hence on $k_0$ and $k'$. Suppose there is an $H$-equivariant $k_0$-algebra section $s:k'\to C/\pi C$ of the residue map. Then there exist a complete discrete valuation ring $V$ with local injective map $W\to V$, an identification $V/\pi V\cong k'$ (so $\pi$ is a uniformizer of $V$), and an $H$-action on $V$ compatible with the given actions on $W$ and $k'$. The map $W\to V$ is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. There is an $H$-equivariant local $W$-algebra homomorphism $\psi:V\to C$ whose reduction modulo $\pi$ is $V\to k'\xrightarrow{s}C/\pi C$. Perfect means bijective Frobenius on $k_0$. No injectivity of $\psi$ is assumed or asserted for general $C$.

source.place: Exposé IV 4.3.5, p.60: Cohen rings I(k′H)→I(k′), lifted residue action and V=W⊗_{W(k0)}I(k′); equivariant lifting by isobarycentres, with square-zero lift torsor Lemma 4.3.6. Formal smoothness and the complete DVR property are the coefficient construction of 4.2.5 and 4.1.3–4.1.8.

proof.text: Put $G=\operatorname{im}(H\to\operatorname{Aut}(k'))$ and $F=(k')^G$. This is a finite group acting faithfully on $k'$, so [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree] gives that $k'/F$ is finite separable. Choose a Cohen ring $D$ with residue field $F$ using [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-rings-exist], and apply [lem-per-finite-etale-cohen-extension] to obtain a Cohen ring $B$ finite etale over $D$ with residue field $k'$. Lift each element of $G$ by its unique $D$-automorphism of $B$. The lift of a product equals the product of the lifts because they induce the same residue automorphism and reduction is injective on automorphisms. The identity lifts to the identity. Composing $H\to G$ gives an $H$-action on $B$, inducing its prescribed action on $k'$. No faithfulness of the original $H$-action is assumed.

source.place: IV 4.3.5, first Cohen-ring paragraph, printed p.60; finite-etale lifting: Stacks Tag 04GK

proof.text: Choose a Cohen ring $A$ for $k_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-rings-exist]. By [lem-per-perfect-cohen-residue-map], every residue automorphism $h:k_0\to k_0$ lifts uniquely to a local endomorphism $\alpha_h$ of $A$. Uniqueness gives $\alpha_h\alpha_g=\alpha_{hg}$ and $\alpha_1=1$, so $\alpha_{h^{-1}}$ is its inverse and these maps define an $H$-action. The same lemma gives local maps $a:A\to W$ and $b:A\to B$ lifting $k_0\xrightarrow{=}W/\pi W$ and $k_0\hookrightarrow k'$. Both $h_W a$ and $a\alpha_h$ induce $h:k_0\to k_0$, so uniqueness gives $h_W a=a\alpha_h$; similarly $h_B b=b\alpha_h$. The rings $W,B,A$ are Noetherian since they are principal ideal domains, and they are complete by their DVR/Cohen hypotheses, as required for that lemma.

source.place: IV 4.1.8–4.1.9, pp.57–58, and 4.3.5: perfect-residue uniqueness gives equivariance

proof.text: Form $V=W\otimes_A B$. By [lem-per-ramified-cohen-tensor-dvr], this is a complete mixed-characteristic DVR, $W\to V$ is local injective and flat, its maximal ideal is generated by $\pi\otimes1$, and $V/\pi V=k'$ with the specified residue inclusion. Define $h(w\otimes z)=h_W(w)\otimes h_B(z)$. It is well-defined: the balancing relation $wa(x)\otimes z=w\otimes b(x)z$ is sent to the balancing relation for $\alpha_h(x)$ by Step 2. Multiplication on pure tensors and the tensor pushout property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] give a ring endomorphism. Checking identity and composition on $w\otimes1$ and $1\otimes z$ gives the group law and inverse. The residue isomorphism is equivariant since its formula is $w\otimes z\mapsto\bar w\bar z$. Thus this action has all required compatibilities.

source.place: IV 4.3.5, V=W′_0 tensor I(k′), printed p.60

proof.text: The extension $k'/k_0$ is formally smooth with the discrete topology. Indeed for a square-zero ideal $J$ in a $k_0$-algebra $E$ and $g:k'\to E/J$, [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-nilpotent-lifting] gives a ring lift $f:k'\to E$. It is $k_0$-linear: if $x=y^p$ in $k_0$ and $i:k_0\to k'$, $c:k_0\to E$ are structure maps, then $f(i(y))-c(y)\in J$ and $f(i(x))-c(x)=(f(i(y))-c(y))^p=0$, because $E$ has characteristic $p$ and $J^2=0$. Perfectness supplies $y$ for every $x$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-formally-smooth-closed-fibre-adic] to $W\to V$, which is local and flat between Noetherian rings by Step 3. Its closed fibre is exactly $k'$ with zero maximal ideal, whose lifting property was just checked. Consequently $W\to V$ is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology.

source.place: IV 4.1.4–4.1.5, p.57, and 4.2.5, p.59; Stacks Tags 0320 and 07NQ

proof.text: Write $I_r=\pi C\cap\mathfrak n^r$ and $E_r=C/I_r$ for $r\ge1$. These ideals are $H$-stable: $h_W(\pi)$ generates $\pi W$, so its image generates $\pi C$, and local automorphisms preserve $\mathfrak n$. The natural maps $E_{r+1}\twoheadrightarrow E_r$ have kernels $J_r=I_r/I_{r+1}$ with $J_r^2=0$: products lie in $\pi C\cap\mathfrak n^{2r}\subset I_{r+1}$. Also $\pi J_r=0$. As $\pi C\subset\mathfrak n$, $E_1=C/\pi C$. Start with $f_1:V\to k'\xrightarrow{s}E_1$, which is equivariant and $W$-linear. Suppose an equivariant $W$-map $f_r:V\to E_r$ compatible with $f_1$ is chosen. It kills $(\pi V)^r$, since $\pi^r C\subset I_r$. Formal smoothness [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] therefore supplies a $W$-algebra lift $u:V\to E_{r+1}$ across the square-zero ideal $J_r$.

source.place: IV 4.3.5, cran par cran, and Lemma 4.3.6, p.60; explicit intersection-ideal tower retaining the prescribed section

proof.text: For each $h\in H$ put $u_h=h\circ u\circ h^{-1}$ and $d_h=u_h-u:V\to J_r$. Equivariance of $f_r$ puts these differences in $J_r$. Each $u_h$ is $W$-linear, despite the semilinear actions, because the actions on $V$ and $E_{r+1}$ agree on $W$. Thus $d_h$ vanishes on $W$ and is additive. Expanding $u_h(x)u_h(y)-u(x)u(y)$ and using $J_r^2=0$ gives $d_h(xy)=u(x)d_h(y)+u(y)d_h(x)$. Conjugation acts on these additive maps; changing the chosen lift $u$ in the scalar action on $J_r$ has no effect because the difference is in $J_r$. The identities $u_{gh}-u=(u_g-u)+g\cdot(u_h-u)$ give $d_{gh}=d_g+g\cdot d_h$. This proves directly the square-zero lift-torsor calculation used here, without a finite-presentation hypothesis.

source.place: IV Lemma 4.3.6, p.60, expanded difference-of-lifts calculation

proof.text: Let $N=|H|$ and set $\delta=N^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}d_h$. The scalar $N^{-1}$ exists in $W$ and its images in all targets are fixed by every ring automorphism. Therefore $\delta$ is additive, vanishes on $W$, has image in $J_r$ and satisfies the same Leibniz rule as the $d_h$. The map $f_{r+1}=u+\delta$ is a unital $W$-algebra homomorphism: its product expansion has the two Leibniz terms and a zero $\delta(x)\delta(y)$ term; it lifts $f_r$. For $g\in H$, the cocycle identity and reindexing $h\mapsto gh$ give $g\cdot\delta=N^{-1}\sum_h(d_{gh}-d_g)=\delta-d_g$, whence $g\cdot f_{r+1}=u+d_g+\delta-d_g=f_{r+1}$. This supplies the equivariant lift at each induction step. Starting from $f_1$ and repeating the construction gives compatible equivariant $f_r$ for all $r\ge1$.

source.place: IV 4.3.5, isobarycentres, and 4.3.6, p.60; explicit averaging formula

proof.text: The canonical map $C\to\varprojlim_r E_r$ is an isomorphism. For injectivity, $\bigcap_r I_r\subset\bigcap_r\mathfrak n^r=0$ by [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. For surjectivity choose representatives $c_r$ of a compatible family. Then $c_{r+1}-c_r\in I_r\subset\mathfrak n^r$, so completeness produces $c\in C$ with $c-c_r\in\mathfrak n^r$. All $c_r$ have the same class in $C/\pi C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient], $C/\pi C$ is separated and complete for its maximal ideal, so the image of $c-c_1$, lying in every power of that ideal, is zero. Hence $c-c_r\in\pi C\cap\mathfrak n^r=I_r$. Ring operations and $H$-actions commute with the quotient maps, so the isomorphism is equivariant. Taking the limit of the $f_r$ yields an equivariant $W$-map $\psi:V\to C$ whose reduction modulo $\pi$ is exactly $f_1=s\circ q_V$. Since the composite to $C/\mathfrak n=k'$ is the residue map of $V$, its inverse image of $\mathfrak n$ is $\pi V$; thus $\psi$ is local. No injectivity assertion for $\psi$ is used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NK-3520d225d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all eight steps against ILO IV 4.1.2–4.1.9 (pp.56–58), 4.2.5 (p.59) and 4.3.5–4.3.6 (p.60), and against Stacks 04GK, 0325 and 07NQ. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, and there is no repair note, so this is an ordinary split. Step 1: G is the image of H in Aut(k'); the fixed-degree leaf gives k'/F finite Galois, and the bijective reduction makes the lifts a group action. Step 2: uniqueness from the perfect-residue map makes a and b equivariant; both composites have the same residue map because W→C is equivariant. Step 3: the tensor node's hypotheses hold, and h_W⊗h_B respects the balancing relation. Step 4: the p-th power argument gives k0-linearity, and the flat closed-fibre criterion (07NQ) applies to the local flat map W→V. Step 5: I_1=πC because π∈n, J_r²⊂I_{r+1}, the ideals are H-stable because h_W(π) is a unit times π, and f_r kills m_V^r. Steps 6–7: the cocycle, Leibniz and averaging identities check, using J_r²=0 and the invariance of N^{-1}. Step 8: C equals the inverse limit of the C/I_r, using the separatedness of C/πC from 0325; ψ is local, and its reduction is f_1. All three new nodes are true, statement-only, smaller than the item and not duplicates. The perfect-residue map node is ILO 4.1.8(i) plus 4.1.9; the existing cohen-ring-lift node gives existence only, and uniqueness is needed. The finite-étale node is B=D[x]/(f̃) with Hensel's lemma; the existing henselian-lift nodes lack the Cohen, DVR and completeness clauses. In the tensor node, W is generated by π over A by an Eisenstein polynomial, which stays Eisenstein over B; the existing coefficient-dvr node is existential and cannot carry the action. I tested small cases: H trivial, W=A, L=F, π=0 in C, and residue fields of characteristic 0. I accept the four generic tool_uses: Cohen-ring existence, field nilpotent lifting, 07NQ and 0325. No changes were made.
